newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: POLL - Dutch July CPI seen up 2.3 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Dutch July CPI seen up 2.3 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Economists expect the Dutch consumer price index (CPI) to have risen 2.3 percent on an annual basis in July, compared with 2.2 percent in June.
They expect the July consumer price index, due to be published on Friday, to show a month-on-month increase of 0.5 percent.
ABN AMRO pointed to a rise in gasoline prices in July, caused by higher taxes, as one reason for the higher CPI.
Rabobank said the annual rise in housing rents, which traditionally occurs on July 1, would push up the yearly figure, while the rise in the monthly figure would reflect higher gasoline prices.
Summer sales for shoes and clothing and lower prices for fresh fruit and vegetables would have a mitigating effect on overall price levels, Rabo said.
Generale Bank said part of the impact of the summer sales had already been absorbed in the June CPI figure.
Forecasts contributed by: ABN AMRO, Generale Bank, ING, MeesPierson, J.P. Morgan, NIB Securities, Rabobank.
